calendar.impact: The airport has been closed under a NOTAM expiring 21:00 GMT Oct 17 after the Houthi strikes. Expiry does not guarantee resumption and no resumption was confirmed by early Saturday; several carriers (Etihad through Oct 19, Air France-KLM through end-October, Philippine Airlines to Nov 29) are suspended well beyond today. Actual resumption is a read on Saudi air-defence confidence after the Yanbu missile was aimed at the East-West pipeline terminus on Friday.

changes.balance: Both benchmarks are now compounding the premium, reversing Thursday's divergence, and part of Friday's bid is an acknowledged weekend-risk premium that gets its verdict at Monday's open. The flow impairment is measured and worsening, which is what separates Friday from a pure headline session.
changes.body: Friday was an escalation session with markets now closed for the weekend. Brent Dec26 settled at $109.86 (+$3.94, +3.7 percent), its highest close since May 19 after touching $110 for the first time since May; WTI Nov26 settled at $101.41 (+$3.44, +3.5 percent), its highest since September 17. On the week WTI gained 10.4 percent and Brent 4.9 percent, and the front Brent-WTI spread widened to $8.45 on settles. Kpler put crude shipments through Hormuz at an average of 9.4 Mb/d for the week ended Wednesday, about 70 percent of the pre-war average, and at least nine tankers and cargo ships have come under attack near the Strait since Sunday. The crude tanker MT ST 3 was struck by a projectile on Friday; all 15 Indian crew are safe. An IRGC claim that an unidentified tanker struck a naval mine is unverified and unlinked to MT ST 3. Market commentary named an explicit weekend-risk premium inside Friday's bid, and Energy Aspects noted part of the reversal ran on rumours and unverified reports.
changes.conditional: A quiet weekend and a soft Monday open -> the weekend component of the premium bleeds out; another vessel strike or a Saudi process hit -> the premium rebuilds as a supply story
changes.delta: Friday settles, Oct 16: Brent Dec26 $109.86 (+$3.94, +3.7%, highest since May 19, $110 touched), WTI Nov26 $101.41 (+$3.44, +3.5%, highest since Sep 17); week WTI +10.4%, Brent +4.9%; front Brent-WTI $8.45. Kpler: Hormuz crude shipments averaged 9.4 Mb/d in the week ended Wednesday, about 70% of the pre-war average; at least nine ships attacked since Sunday; MT ST 3 struck Friday, crew safe
changes.source: Reuters, Oct 16, 2026 (Friday settles and Hormuz reporting); Kpler via Reuters, Oct 16, 2026
changes.title: Friday escalation settle: Brent $109.86, WTI $101.41; Hormuz shipments down to 9.4 Mb/d

changes.balance: The bypass was aimed at and still works, which cuts both ways: Saudi export capacity is intact, and the route the market treated as safe now carries a named-threat premium. Riyadh airport's closure expiry today is the next read on air-defence confidence.
changes.body: On Friday the Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu, the Red Sea terminus of the East-West pipeline and the kingdom's Hormuz bypass, along with two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones over the southern region and Riyadh; Rapidan reported no damage to Yanbu infrastructure. On Friday evening two missiles landed inside Aden International Airport's perimeter while a Yemenia flight prepared to depart; no casualties were reported, and the Houthis said they had targeted a Saudi command headquarters and munitions depot at the adjacent Badr camp. Saudi Arabia accused Iran of encouraging the Houthi escalation; Tehran denied any role on Friday and offered to mediate. Riyadh's King Khalid airport closure notice expires at 21:00 GMT today with no resumption confirmed, and several carriers remain suspended well beyond today.
changes.conditional: A hit on Yanbu, East-West, or a Saudi process asset -> the bypass premium becomes a supply loss; a clean airport resumption and a quiet weekend -> the Saudi leg of the premium fades first
changes.delta: Coalition, Oct 16: ballistic missile intercepted over Yanbu (East-West pipeline terminus), two cruise missiles over the Red Sea, three drones destroyed over the south and Riyadh; no Yanbu infrastructure damage (Rapidan). Two missiles inside Aden airport perimeter Friday evening, no casualties. Iran denied encouraging the Houthi escalation and offered mediation. Riyadh airport NOTAM expires 21:00 GMT Oct 17, resumption unconfirmed
changes.source: Reuters, Oct 16, 2026 (coalition spokesman; Yemeni security officials; Iranian foreign ministry spokesman)
changes.title: Yanbu targeted and intercepted; Aden airport struck again; Tehran denies a role

changes.balance: The crack's regime test now has a scored answer: a sub-$100 close was required and Friday closed $104.35 instead, with a Russian distillation unit halted and US distillate stocks 11.7 percent below the seasonal average. Pledged IEA barrels have not capped the crack; delivered barrels remain the confirmation channel. In Canada the December wide still rests on freight and the unseen November apportionment notice.
changes.body: The diesel crack closed Friday at $104.35 on the validated daily history, a tenth consecutive day above $100 (38 total days; maximum $117.92 on Sep 16), after Thursday morning's $97.30 overnight bar failed to hold on a closing basis; the 3-2-1 closed at $57.77. Industry sources told Reuters a primary crude distillation unit at Ryazan (about 340 kb/d, roughly 5 percent of Russian refining capacity) was halted after Thursday's drone attack, and no Russian diesel cargo has loaded. US retail diesel averaged $6.33 per gallon Friday. The new COT vintage (as of Oct 13, released Friday) diverged: WTI managed-money net fell to +40,574 (about the 25th percentile; shorts rose to 131,399, the largest since December 2025), while Brent net rebuilt to +233,029 (+31,977), the first build in four weeks. Canadian diffs carry Oct 15 ICE settles into the weekend: WCS Dec26 -$26.75 on 805 lots, SYN Nov26 +$7.55 across the Syncrude coker return that wrapped Oct 16, C5 Dec26 +$4.00. AESO Oct 17: all monitored SAGD cogen units at full maximum capability.
changes.conditional: IEA diesel arrivals land and US distillate builds -> the crack regime break finally confirms; SYN settles at or below +$6.50 within three business days -> the Syncrude supply-return read confirms, while a hold above +$7.00 to Oct 23 scores it priced-in or slipped
changes.delta: Diesel crack $104.35 on the completed Oct 16 close (tenth straight day above $100; 3-2-1 $57.77), reversing the $97.30 overnight bar. Ryazan primary distillation unit halted (industry sources, via Reuters). COT as of Oct 13, released Oct 16: WTI net +40,574 (25th percentile, shorts 131,399), Brent net +233,029 (+31,977). WCS Dec26 -$26.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 15, 805 lots); SYN Nov26 +$7.55 into the completed Syncrude coker window

changes.title: Crack closes back above $100 for a tenth day; Ryazan unit halted; specs diverge in the new COT

flags.body: Kpler shipments averaged 9.4 Mb/d in the week ended Wednesday, about 70 percent of the pre-war average, below the 11.62 Mb/d total-clearance average for the seven days to Oct 13. At least nine ships have been attacked since Sunday and MT ST 3 was struck Friday. Brent settled at its highest since May 19. The risk is clearance falling further or a strike hitting Saudi process, pipeline or export assets; Yanbu was already aimed at on Friday and intercepted.

flags.body: The diesel crack closed at $104.35 on Friday, a tenth straight day above $100, after the sub-$100 overnight print failed to hold on a closing basis. The IEA acceleration (remaining roughly 100 Mbbl, 20+ Mbbl of diesel) has no published arrival timing, Ryazan's primary distillation unit is halted, and US distillate stocks are 11.7 percent below the seasonal average. flags.body: No DOE press announcement on the sixth solicitation as of early Saturday, eleven days after the Oct 6 bid deadline, and the DOE solicitation page (Sep 29, updated Oct 5) remains the latest item. DOE's posted contracts tell the program story without one: 133.56 Mbbl already lent to 13 companies across the spring rounds, Trafigura the largest borrower at about 34 Mbbl (25.7 percent), ahead of Marathon (12.4 Mbbl) and ExxonMobil (11.4 Mbbl); trading houses took 45 percent of the total against 38 percent for refiners (posted contracts tallied Oct 13). The pending award adds 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery when it lands.
flags.title: SPR 40 Mbbl award still pending, eleven days after bids

flags.body: Every tanker route repriced violently in the week ending Oct 9 (Baltic weekly, pulled Oct 16). TD22 (US Gulf Coast to China, VLCC) is $40.23/bbl against a Brent-WTI spread of $8.45 (Oct 16 settle): the US export arb is dead at roughly five times the spread, so US barrels stay home and the Gulf gets long the grades WCS clears against. TD28 (Vancouver to China) rose 85 percent to $25.58/bbl, taxing the TMX outlet in the same week. TD9 (Caribbean to US Gulf Coast) printed WS1030, about $19.08/bbl estimated, up 51 percent: high Jose-to-Gulf freight does not shield WCS, it makes Venezuela a captive Gulf seller, so Merey length gets offered into the Gulf at deeper FOB discounts to stay placed, and those walked-down offers pressure WCS Houston whether they fill or not. The confirmation gauge is the Merey FOB discount: while it keeps deepening, the wall is still transmitting.
flags.title: Freight wall: Western heavies reprice together
flags.trigger: TD22 falls back toward the Brent-WTI spread, or TD9 eases and the Merey FOB discount stops deepening
